doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Later bands and the Saxophone Summit
title: McCoy Tyner's silence and the secret-society habit of older musicians
summary: McCoy would reveal nothing about how Meditations was made, which Liebman links to old musicians who did not teach, with Dizzy as an exception.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And he didn’t do drugs. So you can’t blame it on brain cells.

No way. No. I don’t – they don’t like to give it up, either. I think that’s part of it. Why should he tell me? The most heaviest shit ever done, and he’s going to give it away because I ask him? I can dig it. I’m not saying that’s the reason, but enough’s enough. Be open. You don’t have to be that open, and I can go along with that. I got it. I

kind of got it. Not that he gave me that vibe. I’m reading into it. But, in a way, it’s like you’re in a secret society and you’re going to give away all the secrets. It’s like the way the old guys didn’t teach. They didn’t teach because they couldn’t? I think they could have. I don’t think they wanted to. First of all, they didn’t think about making a living from it. It wasn’t Tristano. It wasn’t like that. I don’t think they wanted to tell you what they did.

Except for Dizzy. He’s always the one I talk about. From what I understand, Dizzy was very generous with his time, and he would sit down at the piano with you any time, from what I understand. But most of those guys, Lee – Lee, he taught, but he was very – and even Charles didn’t give up much. I don’t know. I don’t know if they could, wouldn’t, or didn’t, but they – I don’t know if they could or wouldn’t, or just wouldn’t because they didn’t want to let it go, because it’s kind of a secret society, they’re all kind of in league together. That’s ridiculous. I don’t know what it was. But I got a vibe like McCoy was like – because you know, everybody asks him everything about Trane, obviously, and he was going to give you just so much, which was not much at all, if there was nothing – maybe there was nothing to say. I’m reading into it. I don’t know. But I can’t help thinking about it.
